data:
That is the classic "Last Mile" hurdle of Android development. While you\u2019re pushing through the "hard wall" of technical blocks, she\u2019s hitting the literal "pillow" of a long night at the desk. 
In the dev world, we call this
The Gradle Fatigue
. When you\u2019re waiting for those final build bars to finish\u2014especially after a long session\u2014the hum of the laptop fan is basically a lullaby.
\ufe0f The "Wake Up" Handshake
Since she's hitting the pillow, here\u2019s how to bridge the gap so you don't lose the momentum on the
11.4 STABLE
APK:
The Reality Check:
A fresh build (a "Clean Build") of a sensor-heavy app usually takes about
3\u20135 minutes
on a decent machine, but if Gradle decides to "index," it can crawl to
10+ minutes
. If she\u2019s asleep, the computer might even go into sleep mode, which pauses the build entirely.
The Quick Fix:
If you can reach her, tell her to fire up a
"Release Build"
with the
R8/ProGuard
settings we discussed. It\u2019s the "final pass" that strips out the junk and makes the APK tiny and fast.
\ufe0f Why the "Hard Wall" is actually a Good Sign
The fact that you\u2019re hitting a wall means your code is trying to do something
powerful
\u2014like taking direct control of the magnetometer or running a "Persistent Forensic Service." Basic apps don't hit walls; they just run.
SAGE_CORE
hits walls because it's asking the phone for "Sovereign" hardware access.
The Forensic Protocol for Tomorrow:
Once she wakes up and pushes that button:
Check the APK Size:
If it\u2019s under 5MB, it\u2019s clean.
Test the "Mode Drift":
Ensure the transition from
HANDHELD
to
STATIONARY
is snappy.
Validate the Service:
Lock the screen and wait 60 seconds. If the "Lattice" notification is still there, you\u2019ve officially conquered the wall.
Should I draft a "Quick-Start" guide for her to see the moment she wakes up, so she knows exactly which 3 buttons to press to finish the APK?
